Additional sources of bias: Animal model (guinea pig); before/after samples from different sites (cardiac puncture vs heart after thoracotomy); 2 animals per condition; authors note remaining problems with handling of coagulated blood and that human heart blood is better heat-protected (p4–p5)
Notes: Animal 1 of 2 in this condition (row order as printed). Reported CO liberation rate is the condition mean of both animals; calculated % is per animal and differs. Authors (p3): at 300 °C·15 min, 500 °C·10 min and 700 °C·5 min blood stayed fluid and CO release from COHb was at most about 20%; at 300 °C·30 min, 500 °C·20 min and 700 °C·10 min blood heat-coagulated with about 50% release. Fig. 5–6 (p3–p4): product <5000 °C×min → ~18% release, ≥10000 → 50–60% (figure points unlabelled; not extracted). After-heating values without SD printed as single values.
